# Fixtures

- `foreign-site-data.php` stands in for another plugin that owns `voyager/site-data`. `scripts/foreign-owner-check.mjs` installs it for one run.
- `site-data-keys.json` pins what each of the 27 `voyager/site-data` keys resolves to for a set of untidy option values. `scripts/site-data-fixture-check.mjs` runs it against the local site. voyager-blocks carries a byte-identical copy, so both repos must change together. `site-data-keys.sha256` is the pin: `npm run check` fails when the fixture no longer matches it, and voyager-blocks compares its copy against the same hash. Write the options with their `sanitize_option_*` filters removed, as the script does, so the fixture exercises `values()` and not the settings sanitizers.
- `contrast.json` is what `npm run design-check` (`scripts/design-check.mjs`) renders and measures: the section styles and widths every pattern is rendered in, the 4.5:1 floor, the render and pair counts the run must reach, the link put into the CTA band, the motion sample gap, the width each planted control loads at, and per theme the WordPress version it runs on, the commit to install when it is not bundled with WordPress (Ipsum), the role map get-catalog must report, the low-contrast map the contrast control sets, the colour style variations it ships, and the pairs known to measure under the floor, with their ratios. `a11y` holds the axe-core tags and the extra rule (`heading-order`) the a11y check runs. `impeccable` holds the Impeccable rule ids the impeccable check fails on, the 44px tap-target minimum the check measures itself, and per theme the targets known to measure under it, with their heights.
- `palette-slugs.json` lists the palette slugs each built-in section style role map is chosen by: the bundled themes' and the Voyager design system's. `tests/Unit/SectionStylesTest.php` checks every map against it.
- `fold-unreleased/` is the known answer for `scripts/fold-unreleased.mjs`: change notes in `unreleased/`, the `readme.in.txt` they fold into, and the `readme.expected.txt` the fold must write. `scripts/test-fold-unreleased.mjs` runs it on a copy, so the fixture never changes, and `npm run check` runs that test.
- `presets/allowed.html` writes every preset form the presets gate accepts once: colour, gradient, border, overlay and icon colour slugs, `var:preset|…` references and their `var(--wp--preset--…)` form, font size and font family slugs and references, radius, shadow and text shadow references, a duotone preset and `unset`, and spacing slugs 20 to 60. `npm run check` asserts the gate passes it, so a rule grown to refuse a preset turns the check red.
- `purge-recorder.php` records every `voyager_open_blocks_purge` call, with its URLs and context, and serves the records at `/wp-json/voyager-open-blocks-test/v1/purges`. `blueprints/dev.json` installs it as an mu-plugin on the dev site, so `npm run e2e` can check which pages a Site Data or post meta change refreshes.
